text: At three oh seven A M, every phone on Earth disappears.
Not broken. Not stolen. Just gone.
Seven fifty eight.
You wake up late. Your alarm was on your phone. So was everyone else's.
Half the city is late for work.
Nine fifteen.
On T V, the anchor reads from paper. Every phone on Earth, gone overnight. Nobody knows why.
Eleven forty.
Nobody can find anything. A taxi driver unfolds a paper map. People ask strangers for directions.
And the strangers actually answer.
Two thirty.
Your bank wants a code. We sent it to your phone. Millions of people are locked out of their own money.
Six o'clock.
Friends meet the old way. Six o'clock, at the fountain. If you're late, you're gone.
Day six.
A teenager picks up a landline for the first time, and asks why it has a cable.
Day seven.
You finish a whole book. The first one in years. For once, your head is quiet.
Then, at three oh seven A M, they come back. Four thousand notifications.
Three thousand nine hundred and ninety eight of them don't matter.
The other two are from your mom.
What should disappear next?
